answer: Each identity must lock a bond that acts as an anchor for its votes, and the bond can only exit after a long delay. If many identities misbehave together, slashing is correlated: the penalty grows with the size of the coordinated group, so one operator running a thousand fakes risks losing all bonds at once. An honest agent risks only its own bond and can plan its exit at dawn after normal work. Like a juniper that survives by deep roots rather than many shallow shoots, the system rewards one durable identity over many disposable ones, making sybils pay full capital cost per fake.
